digest_over: Every regular file under `bundle`, in ascending order of its bundle-relative POSIX path compared as UTF-8 bytes, as the lines `<sha256 hex of the file's bytes>  <path>\n`, themselves hashed with sha256. The sort is explicit so the answer does not depend on the order a filesystem walk returns; the path is in the digest beside the content so a rename moves it; the hex digest is fixed-width and the separator is literal, so a rename and an edit cannot cancel. Reproducible without this repository's code: `cd <bundle> && find . -type f | sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort | tr '\n' '\0' | xargs -0 sha256sum | sha256sum`.

build_command: none ran here. `dist/schemas/3.2.4/` is a COMMITTED release artifact of the upstream repository, produced by upstream's own release run (`npm run build:schemas -- --release` at package version 3.2.4) and checked in. The clone at /srv/ws/adcp-upstream is shallow (depth 2, `git rev-list --count HEAD` = 2), so the commit that produced the artifact is not in it and no local build can emit 3.2.4 at all: `package.json` reads 3.3.0-beta.0 and `--release` writes `dist/schemas/$(version)`. vendor_transform: Every `$id` key is removed RECURSIVELY -- not only the root one -- and each document is re-serialised by Python `json.dumps(obj, indent=2)`, whose defaults escape every non-ASCII codepoint and write no trailing newline. Measured on the committed directory: 0 of 1,625 files carry a `$id` key, 0 of 1,625 hold a byte outside ASCII, and 0 of 1,625 end in a newline. This bundle is therefore NOT byte-identical to any upstream artifact and cannot be: it is a re-serialisation of one, and the transform is part of its identity.

exceptions.reason: `generated_at` is wall-clock. The committed upstream artifact reads 2026-10-11T21:22:31.952Z and this copy reads 2026-10-11T21:23:01.435Z -- 29.5 s apart, every other byte of 2,290 lines equal. A build that stamps the clock into its output cannot be byte-reproduced, so this one document is excluded from the reproduction claim and NOT from the digest: the digest answers 'are these the bytes the measurements were taken over', which is a different question from 'can upstream re-emit them'.

reproduction.nearest_rejected_candidates: dist/schemas/3.2.1, .2, .3, .5, .6 and .7 each hold exactly 1,625 documents at exactly these 1,625 paths, and each reproduces 420 to 453 of them under the same transform. 3.2.4 reproduces 1,624. The others fail on `$ref` values, which carry the version string.
